title: Warren Soultrader + Gravecrawler + Bastion of Remembrance: is the drain unbounded, and what does one iteration cost?

Bastion of Remembrance's triggered ability — 'Whenever a creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life.' Triggered on Gravecrawler's death during cost payment.

assumptions: No player responds to anything; every opponent passes priority throughout.
No permanent enters or leaves the battlefield except as described by the cards named here.
It is your precombat main phase, so you have sorcery-speed permission when you hold priority with an empty stack.

extras.note_for_the_resolver: This is the deck's declared FOURTH KILL and it has never been resolved. combo_details.json records the line as 'Infinite lifeloss'; that is a containment tag from Commander Spellbook and not a verification. The board is deliberately minimal — no Nest of Scarabs, no Blowfly Infestation, no commander, no floating mana — because the question is whether the loop funds itself. Note the Treasure token created by the ability on the stack is an artifact, not a creature.

scenario.question: Resolve the stack, then resolve one full further iteration of the loop. (1) Can the loop be repeated an unbounded number of times from this board with no mana or life from outside it — specifically, does casting Gravecrawler from the graveyard have a legal permission each time, and does the Treasure created by each activation pay for that cast? (2) What is the exact net change per completed iteration to your life total, to each opponent's life total, and to the number of Treasures you control?

steps.action: Establish the stack order before anyone passes priority. Warren Soultrader's activated ability was put on the stack first (pos 0); its costs — pay 1 life, sacrifice another creature — were then paid, and Gravecrawler's death during that cost payment triggered Bastion of Remembrance. A triggered ability does nothing at the moment it triggers; it is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, i.e. after activation is complete, so it lands ON TOP of the ability that caused it (pos 1).

steps.action: All players pass again. Warren Soultrader's activated ability resolves: create a Treasure token. Establish here, once, why nothing further triggers — this is what caps the drain at exactly 1 per iteration. A triggered ability triggers only when a game event or game state MATCHES its trigger event. Bastion of Remembrance has exactly two triggered abilities: 'When this enchantment enters, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token' (its entry is long past) and 'Whenever a creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life'. Bastion has no trigger event of the form 'a permanent enters' or 'a creature enters' at all, so creating a token — of any kind — matches neither ability. Creating the Treasure is therefore not a trigger event for Bastion, and the same rule governs steps 7 and 8 below.
steps.effect: You create one Treasure token, an artifact token you control with "{T}, Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color." No ability triggers on its creation. Because the Treasure is an artifact and not a creature, its later sacrifice will not be a creature you control dying either, so it will not match Bastion's death trigger (applied at step 7). Treasures: 0 → 1. The stack is now empty. STACK AS GIVEN IS FULLY RESOLVED: you 40, each opponent 39, Treasures 1, Gravecrawler in graveyard, Warren Soultrader and Bastion of Remembrance on the battlefield.

steps.action: ITERATION 1, part (1) of the question — permission to cast Gravecrawler from the graveyard. Before you receive that priority the game checks state-based actions and performs none: with the stack empty the board is you at 40, each opponent at 39, Warren Soultrader and Bastion of Remembrance on the battlefield and the newly created Treasure on the battlefield as well, so no listed condition is met and no triggered ability is waiting to be put on the stack; the check therefore performs nothing and priority is handed back. You then receive priority with an empty stack in your precombat main phase; the phase does not end merely because the stack emptied. Gravecrawler's own static ability reads 'You may cast this card from your graveyard as long as you control a Zombie.' Two rules are needed, not one. 113.6f is the rule that makes an ability of this kind — one that modifies which zones that object can be cast from — function everywhere, including from the graveyard; without it, appealing to 604.6 alone would be circular, since the graveyard is a zone you could cast Gravecrawler from ONLY because of this very ability. 604.6 then describes the ordinary operation of such a static ability in that zone, and 601.3 is what the permission is needed for. The Zombie condition is met by Warren Soultrader, whose printed type line is Creature — Zombie Goblin Wizard; Soultrader is never sacrificed by this loop (its own ability requires sacrificing ANOTHER creature), so the permission is available on every iteration.
steps.effect: Casting Gravecrawler from the graveyard is legal now and on every future iteration: a noninstant spell, your main phase, stack empty, priority held, permission granted by the card's own ability, which functions in the graveyard by 113.6f, with the Zombie requirement satisfied by the untouched Warren Soultrader.

steps.action: ITERATION 1, part (1) continued — does the Treasure pay for the cast? Gravecrawler's mana cost is {B}. First establish that the Treasure's ability, '{T}, Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color', qualifies as a mana ability: it is an activated ability, it requires no target, it could add mana to your mana pool when it resolves, and it is not a loyalty ability — the three criteria of 605.1a, all met. Because it IS a mana ability, you may activate it while casting Gravecrawler, before costs are paid, and it does not use the stack. The Treasure is an artifact token, not a creature, so the summoning-sickness restriction — written only for a creature's activated ability with the tap symbol — does not reach it even though it was created this turn. Sacrificing it is not a creature you control dying, so no game event matches Bastion's trigger event (the rule stated at step 5) and Bastion does not trigger.
steps.effect: {B} is added to your mana pool and spent on Gravecrawler's total cost. Treasures: 1 → 0. The sacrificed Treasure is a TOKEN now in a zone other than the battlefield, so it ceases to exist — this is the one state-based action this loop actually performs, and it happens at the next check, i.e. when a player would next receive priority once the cast is complete (the check stated at step 8). Nothing in part (2)'s ledger turns on that timing: the number of Treasures you control fell to 0 the moment the token left the battlefield. The same rule's parenthetical is why the trigger analysis above is safe — any applicable triggered ability would trigger BEFORE the token ceased to exist, and none is applicable, because Bastion's trigger event is a creature you control dying. No Bastion trigger. Gravecrawler is on the stack. Exactly one Treasure funds exactly one cast — the mana ledger of one iteration balances at zero.

steps.action: ANSWER TO PART (1) — is the loop unbounded from this board with no outside mana or life? Every resource an iteration consumes it also replaces, in the same iteration, from inside the loop: the {B} for Gravecrawler comes from the Treasure the previous activation made, whose ability is a mana ability (steps 5, 7, 12); the 1 life for Soultrader comes back from Bastion (steps 9, 11); Gravecrawler is a card, so it returns to the graveyard each time and its own ability functions there (steps 6, 9); the Zombie that grants the graveyard permission is Warren Soultrader, which the loop never sacrifices (step 6). Nothing in the loop draws on the three tapped Swamps, the empty hand, or the library. The loop is therefore repeatable an unbounded number of times, and because it can be repeated indefinitely the shortcut rules let you declare a number of iterations rather than perform them.
steps.effect: YES on both halves of part (1): the graveyard cast has a legal permission on every iteration, and each activation's Treasure exactly funds the next cast. The loop is self-funding and unbounded in the rules sense; in practice it terminates because the drain is not — the operative threshold is 0 life, so 40 drain events bring a 40-life opponent to exactly 0, and one drain has already resolved on the stack as given, leaving 39 further iterations after step 5 to put all four opponents at 0 simultaneously, whereupon each of them loses the game. 'Infinite lifeloss' as a containment tag is CONFIRMED for this board, with the arithmetic that matters: 1 life per opponent per iteration, 4 across the pod per iteration, 40 drain events to kill each seat.

final_state.summary: The stack as given resolves top-down: Bastion of Remembrance's trigger first (each opponent 40 → 39, you 39 → 40), then Warren Soultrader's ability, creating one Treasure. One full further iteration — cast Gravecrawler from the graveyard for {B} paid by sacrificing that Treasure, then pay 1 life and sacrifice Gravecrawler to Soultrader — leaves each opponent at 38 and returns the board to an identical state. Both halves of part (1) are YES: Gravecrawler's own ability modifies which zone it can be cast from and so functions in the graveyard (113.6f), granting permission on every iteration with its Zombie condition met by Warren Soultrader, which the loop never sacrifices ('another creature'); and each activation's Treasure exactly funds the next {B}, its ability meeting the definition of a mana ability (605.1a) and being unrestricted because a Treasure is an artifact, not a creature. Exactly one Bastion trigger occurs per iteration: only Gravecrawler's death matches its trigger event, so neither creating nor sacrificing a Treasure adds drain (603.2). Part (2): per completed iteration your life is net 0 (dipping to 39 and refunded), each opponent is −1, and Treasures are net 0 (steady state 1). The loop is self-funding and unbounded; 40 drain events bring a seat to exactly 0 — one has already resolved, so 39 further iterations take all four opponents to 0 at once. The Commander Spellbook tag 'Infinite lifeloss' is confirmed for this exact board.
